events.factual_description: Sumida Triphony Hall presents Miho Hazama with the Danish Radio Big Band on November 18, 2026 at 7:00 PM in the Main Hall. The program includes Jim McNeely's arrangement of 'Sing, Sing, Sing' and Hazama's 'And the Door Unsealed' and 'The First Notes' from the 2026 album Frames. Hazama's official schedule identifies the Tokyo date as part of the Danish Radio Big Band Japan Tour 2026, and Universal Music Japan describes Frames as her new collaboration with the ensemble she leads as chief conductor.

en.why_it_matters: This clears the S bar because it puts one of Japan's most distinctive contemporary jazz composer-conductors in front of the actual European large ensemble she leads, performing music from their current Frames collaboration in Tokyo. The point is not simply that Hazama is acclaimed: this is her compositional language realized at full big-band scale by the orchestra whose history and sound she is actively reshaping. That combination of Japanese authorship, international ensemble identity and current repertoire is unusually strong Listening Notes material.
en.trip_verdict: S within Greater Tokyo/Kanto. Protect the night and cross Tokyo for it, especially if the trip is following the living Japanese jazz language beyond piano-trio and club formats. It stops short of S+ because this is one stop on a seven-date Japan tour rather than a singular one-off, but the Tokyo performance is a serious destination event within Kanto.

es.why_it_matters: Cruza el umbral S porque pone a una de las compositoras-directoras japonesas más distintivas del jazz contemporáneo al frente del ensamble europeo que realmente dirige, tocando en Tokio la música de su colaboración actual Frames. La razón no es simplemente que Hazama tenga prestigio: aquí su lenguaje compositivo aparece a escala completa de big band, interpretado por la orquesta cuya historia y sonido ella está ayudando a transformar. Ese cruce entre autoría japonesa, identidad internacional del ensamble y repertorio vivo es material muy cabrón para Listening Notes.
es.trip_verdict: S dentro de Greater Tokyo/Kanto. Vale proteger la noche y cruzar Tokio por este concierto, sobre todo si el viaje quiere seguir el lenguaje vivo del jazz japonés más allá del formato de trío y de club. No llega a S+ porque forma parte de una gira japonesa de siete fechas y no es una aparición única, pero dentro de Kanto sí funciona como evento-destino serio.
